We emphasize that, in contrast to Theorem 3, in Theorem 5 we require early stopping for some δ>0\delta>0, which in turn leads to the exponential-then-constant step size schedule. We now elaborate on the difference between Theorem 5 and Theorem 3, and provide some intuition for the appearance of the two additional terms in Eqn. (96).

Remark 3.

To obtain an accurate sampler, it is natural to require that Q^t≈Q←t\widehat{Q}_{t}\approx\overset{\leftarrow}{Q}_{t} uniformly for all t∈[0,T]t\in[0,T]. The main challenge is that we only have access to score estimates at discrete time points. In the truncated τ\tau-leaping algorithm analyzed in this section, this results in approximating

s^T−t≔s^T−tk≈sT−t.\displaystyle\widehat{s}_{T-t}\coloneqq\widehat{s}_{T-t_{k}}\approx s_{T-t}.

Informally, we establish this by showing

s^T−tk≈sT−tk≈sT−t,\displaystyle\widehat{s}_{T-t_{k}}\approx s_{T-t_{k}}\approx s_{T-t}, (99)

where the first approximation is ensured by Assumption 1 and the second results from the properties of the score function for the masking noising process, requiring the step size tk+1−tkt_{k+1}-t_{k} to be small.

In contrast, for Algorithm 1 considered in Theorem 3, the condition Q^t≈Q←t\widehat{Q}_{t}\approx\overset{\leftarrow}{Q}_{t} translates to

s^T−t≔eT−tk−1eT−t−1​s^T−tk≈sT−t.\displaystyle\widehat{s}_{T-t}\coloneqq\frac{e^{T-t_{k}}-1}{e^{T-t}-1}\widehat{s}_{T-t_{k}}\approx s_{T-t}.

In view of Proposition 6, the above condition is equivalent to

s^T−t≔eT−tk−1eT−t−1​s^T−tk≈eT−tk−1eT−t−1​sT−tk=sT−t,\displaystyle\widehat{s}_{T-t}\coloneqq\frac{e^{T-t_{k}}-1}{e^{T-t}-1}\widehat{s}_{T-t_{k}}\approx\frac{e^{T-t_{k}}-1}{e^{T-t}-1}s_{T-t_{k}}=s_{T-t},

which is guaranteed by Assumption 1. Notably, this simple rescaling eliminates the need for the second approximation step that is required in the truncated τ\tau-leaping analysis. This distinction explains why Theorem 5 contains two additional error terms and necessitates early stopping, in contrast to the cleaner guarantee obtained in Theorem 3.

Proof of Theorem 5.  The proof follows the proof of Theorem 3 closely with several additional steps. We begin with Equation 91

𝖪𝖫(q←T∥pT)\displaystyle\mathsf{KL}(\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{T}\|p_{T})
≲e−T​d​log⁡S+∑k=0N−1∫tktk+1𝔼xtk,xt∼q←tk,t​∑y≠xt[Q^t​(xt,y)−Q←t​(xt,y)+Q←t​(xt,y)​log⁡(Q←t​(xt,y)Q^t​(xt,y))]​𝑑t.\displaystyle\lesssim e^{-T}d\log S+\!\!\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\int_{t_{k}}^{t_{k+1}}\!\!{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t_{k}},x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{{t_{k},t}}}\sum_{y\neq x_{t}}\left[\widehat{Q}_{t}(x_{t},y)-\overset{\leftarrow}{Q}_{t}(x_{t},y)+\overset{\leftarrow}{Q}_{t}(x_{t},y)\log\left(\frac{\overset{\leftarrow}{Q}_{t}(x_{t},y)}{\widehat{Q}_{t}(x_{t},y)}\right)\right]\mathrm{d}t. (100)

Next, since for this sampler, the rate matrices Q^t\widehat{Q}_{t} are given by the following:

Q^t​(x,y)≔{s^T−tk(xtk⊙iyi,xtk)𝕀{xi=MASK},if d_H(x,y)=1,xi≠yi, and xtki=MASK,−∑z≠xQ^t(x,z),if ​y=x,0,otherwise,\displaystyle\widehat{Q}_{t}(x,y)\coloneqq\begin{cases}\widehat{s}_{T-t_{k}}(x_{t_{k}}\odot_{i}y^{i},x_{t_{k}}){\mathbb{I}}\{x^{i}=\mathrm{MASK}\},&\quad\text{if }\ham(x,y)=1,x^{i}\neq y^{i},\text{ and }x_{t_{k}}^{i}=\mathrm{MASK},\\ -\sum_{z\neq x}\widehat{Q}_{t}(x,z),&\quad\text{if }y=x,\\ 0,&\quad\text{otherwise,}\\ \end{cases}

we can therefore bound

∑y≠xt[Q^t​(xt,y)−Q←t​(xt,y)+Q←t​(xt,y)​log⁡(Q←t​(xt,y)Q^t​(xt,y))]\displaystyle\sum_{y\neq x_{t}}\left[\widehat{Q}_{t}(x_{t},y)-\overset{\leftarrow}{Q}_{t}(x_{t},y)+\overset{\leftarrow}{Q}_{t}(x_{t},y)\log\left(\frac{\overset{\leftarrow}{Q}_{t}(x_{t},y)}{\widehat{Q}_{t}(x_{t},y)}\right)\right]
=∑i∈m⁡(xt)∑c∈[S][Q^t​(xt,xt⊙ic)−Q←t​(xt,xt⊙ic)+Q←t​(xt,xt⊙ic)​log⁡(Q←t​(xt,xt⊙ic)Q^t​(xt,xt⊙ic))]\displaystyle\kern 5.0pt=\sum_{i\in m(x_{t})}\sum_{c\in[S]}\left[\widehat{Q}_{t}(x_{t},x_{t}\odot_{i}c)-\overset{\leftarrow}{Q}_{t}(x_{t},x_{t}\odot_{i}c)+\overset{\leftarrow}{Q}_{t}(x_{t},x_{t}\odot_{i}c)\log\left(\frac{\overset{\leftarrow}{Q}_{t}(x_{t},x_{t}\odot_{i}c)}{\widehat{Q}_{t}(x_{t},x_{t}\odot_{i}c)}\right)\right]
=∑i∈m⁡(xt)∑c∈[S][s^T−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)−sT−t​(xt⊙ic,xt)+sT−t​(xt⊙ic,xt)​log⁡(sT−t​(xt⊙ic,xt)s^T−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ))]\displaystyle\kern 5.0pt=\sum_{i\in m(x_{t})}\sum_{c\in[S]}\left[\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})-s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t})+s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t})\log\left(\frac{s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t})}{\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})}\right)\right]
=∑i∈m⁡(xt)∑c∈[S]sT−t​(xt⊙ic,xt)​D​(s^T−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ),sT−t​(xt⊙ic,xt)).\displaystyle\kern 5.0pt=\sum_{i\in m(x_{t})}\sum_{c\in[S]}s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t})D\left(\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell}),s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t})\right).

To proceed, we again apply the law of cosines D⁡(α,γ)=D⁡(α,β)+D⁡(β,γ)+(α−β)​β−γβ​γD(\alpha,\gamma)=D(\alpha,\beta)+D(\beta,\gamma)+(\alpha-\beta)\frac{\beta-\gamma}{\beta\gamma} with

α=s^T−ℓ(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ),β=sT−ℓ(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ),andγ=sT−t(xt⊙ic,xt).\displaystyle\alpha=\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell}),\qquad\beta=s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell}),\quad\text{and}\quad\gamma=s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t}).

In the following, we slightly abuse the notation and write xt≔(xt⊙ic,xt)x_{t}\coloneqq(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t}) and xℓ≔(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)x_{\ell}\coloneqq(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell}) whenever i∈m⁡(xt)i\in m(x_{t}) and c∈[S]c\in[S] are fixed. As a result, for fixed i,ci,c, one has

sT−t​(xt)​D​(s^T−ℓ​(xℓ),sT−t​(xt))\displaystyle s_{T-t}(x_{t})D\left(\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}),s_{T-t}(x_{t})\right)
=sT−t​(xt)​D​(s^T−ℓ​(xℓ),sT−ℓ​(xℓ))+sT−t​(xt)​D​(sT−ℓ​(xℓ),sT−t​(xt))\displaystyle=s_{T-t}(x_{t})D(\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}),s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}))+s_{T-t}(x_{t})D\left(s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}),s_{T-t}(x_{t})\right)
+s^T−ℓ​(xℓ)−sT−ℓ​(xℓ)sT−ℓ​(xℓ)​(sT−ℓ​(xℓ)−sT−t​(xt)).\displaystyle\qquad+\frac{\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})-s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}{s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}\left(s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})-s_{T-t}(x_{t})\right).

This can be rearranged as follows:

sT−t​(xt)​D​(s^T−ℓ​(xℓ),sT−t​(xt))\displaystyle s_{T-t}(x_{t})D\left(\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}),s_{T-t}(x_{t})\right) =sT−ℓ​(xℓ)​D​(s^T−ℓ​(xℓ),sT−ℓ​(xℓ))⏟≕T1\displaystyle=\underbrace{s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})D(\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}),s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}))}_{\eqqcolon\,T_{1}}
+sT−t​(xt)​D​(sT−ℓ​(xℓ),sT−t​(xt))⏟≕T2\displaystyle\quad+\underbrace{s_{T-t}(x_{t})D\left(s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}),s_{T-t}(x_{t})\right)}_{\eqqcolon\,T_{2}}
+(sT−ℓ​(xℓ)−sT−t​(xt))​log⁡s^T−ℓ​(xℓ)sT−ℓ​(xℓ)⏟≕T3.\displaystyle\qquad+\underbrace{\left(s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})-s_{T-t}(x_{t})\right)\log\frac{\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}{s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}}_{\eqqcolon\,T_{3}}.

It is therefore sufficient to control each term separately. Similar to the proof of Theorem 3, the first term, T1T_{1}, after the summation is upper bounded by the score entropy loss

𝔼xt,xℓ∼q←t,ℓ​∑i∈m⁡(xt)∑c∈[S]sT−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)​D​(s^T−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ),sT−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ))\displaystyle{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t},x_{\ell}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t,\ell}}\sum_{i\in m(x_{t})}\sum_{c\in[S]}s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})D(\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell}),s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell}))
≤𝔼xℓ∼q←ℓ​∑i∈m⁡(xℓ)∑c∈[S]sT−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)​D​(s^T−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ),sT−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ))\displaystyle\quad\leq{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{\ell}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{\ell}}\sum_{i\in m(x_{\ell})}\sum_{c\in[S]}s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})D(\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell}),s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell}))
=ℒSE​(T−ℓ,s^T−ℓ,sT−ℓ),\displaystyle\quad={\mathcal{L}}_{\mathrm{SE}}(T-\ell,\widehat{s}_{T-\ell},s_{T-\ell}),

and, by Assumption 1,

∑k=0N−1∫tktk+1ℒSE​(T−ℓ,s^T−ℓ,sT−ℓ)​𝑑t≤εscore.\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\int_{t_{k}}^{t_{k+1}}{\mathcal{L}}_{\mathrm{SE}}(T-\ell,\widehat{s}_{T-\ell},s_{T-\ell})\mathrm{d}t\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}}. (101)

Now, we turn to controlling the terms T2T_{2} and T3T_{3} which require a different treatment than in the proof of Theorem 3.

For the term T2T_{2}, we again apply the law of cosines with

α=sT−ℓ(xℓ),β=sT−t(xℓ),andγ=sT−t(xt).\displaystyle\alpha=s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}),\qquad\beta=s_{T-t}(x_{\ell}),\quad\text{and}\quad\gamma=s_{T-t}(x_{t}).

This leads to the following decomposition

sT−t​(xt)​D​(sT−ℓ​(xℓ),sT−t​(xt))=sT−t​(xt)​D​(sT−ℓ​(xℓ),sT−t​(xℓ))⏟≕T21+sT−t​(xt)​D​(sT−t​(xℓ),sT−t​(xt))⏟≕T22+(sT−t​(xℓ)−sT−t​(xt))​sT−ℓ​(xℓ)−sT−t​(xℓ)sT−t​(xℓ)⏟≕T23.\displaystyle\begin{aligned} s_{T-t}(x_{t})D(s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}),s_{T-t}(x_{t}))&=\underbrace{s_{T-t}(x_{t})D(s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}),s_{T-t}(x_{\ell}))}_{\eqqcolon\,T_{21}}\\ &\quad+\underbrace{s_{T-t}(x_{t})D(s_{T-t}(x_{\ell}),s_{T-t}(x_{t}))}_{\eqqcolon\,T_{22}}\\ &\qquad+\underbrace{(s_{T-t}(x_{\ell})-s_{T-t}(x_{t}))\frac{s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})-s_{T-t}(x_{\ell})}{s_{T-t}(x_{\ell})}}_{\eqqcolon\,T_{23}}.\end{aligned}
  • •

    For T21T_{21}, using Equation 60, observe that

    D⁡(sT−ℓ​(xℓ),sT−t​(xℓ))\displaystyle D(s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}),s_{T-t}(x_{\ell})) =eT−t−1eT−ℓ−1−1−log⁡eT−t−1eT−ℓ−1≤(eT−ℓ−eT−t)22​(eT−ℓ−1)​(eT−t−1)≲κ2,\displaystyle=\frac{e^{T-t}-1}{e^{T-\ell}-1}-1-\log\frac{e^{T-t}-1}{e^{T-\ell}-1}\leq\frac{(e^{T-\ell}-e^{T-t})^{2}}{2(e^{T-\ell}-1)(e^{T-t}-1)}\lesssim\kappa^{2},

    ∑k=0N−1∫tktk+1𝔼xt,xtk∼q←t,tk​∑i∈m⁡(xt)∑c∈[S]sT−t​(xt⊙ic,xt)​D​(sT−tk​(xtk⊙ic,xtk),sT−t​(xtk⊙ic,xtk))​𝑑t\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\int_{t_{k}}^{t_{k+1}}\!\!{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t},x_{t_{k}}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t,t_{k}}}\!\!\sum_{i\in m(x_{t})}\sum_{c\in[S]}\!s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t})D(s_{T-t_{k}}(x_{t_{k}}\odot_{i}c,x_{t_{k}}),s_{T-t}(x_{t_{k}}\odot_{i}c,x_{t_{k}}))\mathrm{d}t
    ≲κ3​∑k=0N−1𝔼xt∼q←t​∑i∈m⁡(xt)∑c∈[S]sT−t​(xt⊙ic,xt)\displaystyle\quad\lesssim\kappa^{3}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t}}\sum_{i\in m(x_{t})}\sum_{c\in[S]}s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t})

    as ∑c∈[S]qt​(xt⊙ic)=qt​(xt)\sum_{c\in[S]}q_{t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c)=q_{t}(x_{t}).

    The term T22T_{22} is identical to the term T2T_{2} from the proof of Theorem 3, thus we use Lemma 15 and obtain that after summation of over i∈m⁡(xt)i\in m(x_{t}) and c∈[S]c\in[S]:

    ∑k=0N−1∫tktk+1𝔼xtk,xt∼q←tk,t​∑i∈m⁡(xt)∑c∈[S]sT−t​(xt⊙ic,xt)​D​(sT−t​(xtk⊙ic,xtk),sT−t​(xt⊙ic,xt))​𝑑t.\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\int_{t_{k}}^{t_{k+1}}{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t_{k}},x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t_{k},t}}\sum_{i\in m(x_{t})}\sum_{c\in[S]}s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t})D\left(s_{T-t}(x_{t_{k}}\odot_{i}c,x_{t_{k}}),s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t})\right)\mathrm{d}t.

    sT−ℓ​(xℓ)−sT−t​(xℓ)sT−t​(xℓ)=eT−t−eT−ℓeT−ℓ−1,\displaystyle\frac{s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})-s_{T-t}(x_{\ell})}{s_{T-t}(x_{\ell})}=\frac{e^{T-t}-e^{T-\ell}}{e^{T-\ell}-1},

    and importantly it does not depend on xℓx_{\ell}. This implies that upon summation over i∈m⁡(xt)i\in m(x_{t}) and c∈[S]c\in[S], the term T23T_{23} contributes zero, i.e.,

    ∑i∈m⁡(xt)∑c∈[S](sT−t​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)−sT−t​(xt⊙ic,xt))​eT−t−eT−ℓeT−ℓ−1\displaystyle\sum_{i\in m(x_{t})}\sum_{c\in[S]}(s_{T-t}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})-s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t}))\frac{e^{T-t}-e^{T-\ell}}{e^{T-\ell}-1}
    =eT−t−eT−ℓeT−ℓ−1​∑i∈m⁡(xt)(∑c∈[S]qt​(xℓ⊙ic)qt​(xℓ)−∑c∈[S]qt​(xt⊙ic)qt​(xt))\displaystyle\quad=\frac{e^{T-t}-e^{T-\ell}}{e^{T-\ell}-1}\sum_{i\in m(x_{t})}\left(\frac{\sum_{c\in[S]}q_{t}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c)}{q_{t}(x_{\ell})}-\frac{\sum_{c\in[S]}q_{t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c)}{q_{t}(x_{t})}\right)
    =eT−t−eT−ℓeT−ℓ−1​∑i∈m⁡(xt)(1−1)\displaystyle\quad=\frac{e^{T-t}-e^{T-\ell}}{e^{T-\ell}-1}\sum_{i\in m(x_{t})}\left(1-1\right)
    =0.\displaystyle\quad=0.

Putting pieces together, we can conclude

∑k=0N−1∫tktk+1𝔼xtk,xt∼q←tk,t​∑i∈m⁡(xt)∑c∈[S]T2≤κ3​N​d+∑k=0N−1hk+1​∫T−tk+1T−tkℐ⁡(t)​𝑑t.\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\int_{t_{k}}^{t_{k+1}}\!\!{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t_{k}},x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{{t_{k},t}}}\sum_{i\in m(x_{t})}\sum_{c\in[S]}T_{2}\leq\kappa^{3}Nd+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}h_{k+1}\int_{T-t_{k+1}}^{T-t_{k}}{\mathcal{I}}(t)\mathrm{d}t. (104)

It therefore remains to control term T3T_{3}. Recall the definition

T3≔(sT−ℓ​(xℓ)−sT−t​(xt))​log⁡s^T−ℓ​(xℓ)sT−ℓ​(xℓ).\displaystyle T_{3}\coloneqq\left(s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})-s_{T-t}(x_{t})\right)\log\frac{\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}{s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}.

Crucially, unlike in the proof of Theorem 3, we no longer have a martingale property for this term. However, we can decompose

T3=(sT−ℓ​(xℓ)−sT−t​(xℓ))​log⁡s^T−ℓ​(xℓ)sT−ℓ​(xℓ)+(sT−t​(xℓ)−sT−t​(xt))​log⁡s^T−ℓ​(xℓ)sT−ℓ​(xℓ)⏟contributes zero by Lemma 14.\displaystyle T_{3}=\left(s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})-s_{T-t}(x_{\ell})\right)\log\frac{\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}{s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}+\underbrace{\left(s_{T-t}(x_{\ell})-s_{T-t}(x_{t})\right)\log\frac{\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}{s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}}_{\text{contributes zero by~\lx@cref{creftypecap~refnum}{lem:mask_mart}}}.

It remains to bound the first term, which can be written as

(sT−ℓ​(xℓ)−sT−t​(xℓ))​log⁡s^T−ℓ​(xℓ)sT−ℓ​(xℓ)=eT−t−eT−ℓeT−t−1​sT−ℓ​(xℓ)​log⁡s^T−ℓ​(xℓ)sT−ℓ​(xℓ).\displaystyle\left(s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})-s_{T-t}(x_{\ell})\right)\log\frac{\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}{s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}=\frac{e^{T-t}-e^{T-\ell}}{e^{T-t}-1}s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})\log\frac{\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}{s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell})}.

In view of the step size assumption tk+1−tk≤κ​min⁡(1,T−tk+1)t_{k+1}-t_{k}\leq\kappa\min(1,T-t_{k+1}), it satisfies

|eT−t−eT−ℓeT−t−1|≲κ.\displaystyle\left\lvert\frac{e^{T-t}-e^{T-\ell}}{e^{T-t}-1}\right\rvert\lesssim\kappa.

The total contribution of terms T3T_{3} can therefore be upper bounded by the following:

κ​∑k=0N−1∫tktk+1𝔼xℓ∼q←ℓ​∑i∈m⁡(xℓ)∑c∈[S]sT−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)​|log⁡s^T−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)sT−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)|​𝑑t\displaystyle\kappa\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\int_{t_{k}}^{t_{k+1}}{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{\ell}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{\ell}}\sum_{i\in m(x_{\ell})}\sum_{c\in[S]}s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})\left\lvert\log\frac{\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})}{s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})}\right\rvert\mathrm{d}t
=κ​∑k=0N−1(tk+1−tk)​𝔼xℓ∼q←ℓ​∑i∈m⁡(xℓ)∑c∈[S]sT−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)​|log⁡s^T−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)sT−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)|.\displaystyle=\kappa\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}(t_{k+1}-t_{k}){\mathbb{E}}_{x_{\ell}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{\ell}}\sum_{i\in m(x_{\ell})}\sum_{c\in[S]}s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})\left\lvert\log\frac{\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})}{s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})}\right\rvert. (105)

Collecting Eqns. (100), (101), (102), (106), and (105) proves

𝖪𝖫(qδ∥pT−δ)≲εscore+e−Tdlog(S)+∑k=0N−1hk+1∫T−tk+1T−tkℐ(t)dt+κ3Nd+κC,\displaystyle\mathsf{KL}(q_{\delta}\,\|\,p_{T-\delta})\lesssim\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}}+e^{-T}d\log(S)+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}h_{k+1}\int_{T-t_{k+1}}^{T-t_{k}}{\mathcal{I}}(t)\mathrm{d}t+\kappa^{3}Nd+\kappa C,

where

C≔∑k=0N−1(tk+1−tk)​𝔼xℓ∼q←ℓ​∑i∈m⁡(xℓ)∑c∈[S]sT−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)​|log⁡s^T−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)sT−ℓ​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)|.\displaystyle C\coloneqq\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}(t_{k+1}-t_{k}){\mathbb{E}}_{x_{\ell}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{\ell}}\sum_{i\in m(x_{\ell})}\sum_{c\in[S]}s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})\left\lvert\log\frac{\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})}{s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})}\right\rvert.

For our step size schedule, as in Corollary 2, we upper bound

∑k=0N−1hk+1​∫T−tk+1T−tkℐ⁡(t)​𝑑t≤κ​∑k=0N−1∫T−tk+1T−tkmin⁡(1,T−tk+1)​ℐ​(t)​𝑑t≤κ​∫δTmin⁡(1,t)​ℐ​(t)​𝑑t≤κ​𝒟​(qdata).\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}h_{k+1}\int_{T-t_{k+1}}^{T-t_{k}}{\mathcal{I}}(t)\mathrm{d}t\leq\kappa\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\int_{T-t_{k+1}}^{T-t_{k}}\min(1,T-t_{k+1}){\mathcal{I}}(t)\mathrm{d}t\leq\kappa\int_{\delta}^{T}\min(1,t){\mathcal{I}}(t)\mathrm{d}t\leq\kappa{\mathcal{D}}(q_{\mathrm{data}}). (106)

Plugging in the choices κ=O⁡(T+log⁡(δ−1)N)\kappa=O\left(\frac{T+\log(\delta^{-1})}{N}\right), T=O⁡(log⁡(ε−1​d​log⁡S))T=O(\log(\varepsilon^{-1}d\log S)), and

N=O~​(𝒟⁡(qdata)+Cε+dε),\displaystyle N=\widetilde{O}\left(\frac{{\mathcal{D}}(q_{\mathrm{data}})+C}{\varepsilon}+\sqrt{\frac{d}{\varepsilon}}\right),

yields 𝖪𝖫(qδ∥pT−δ)≲εscore+ε.\mathsf{KL}(q_{\delta}\|p_{T-\delta})\lesssim\varepsilon_{\mathrm{score}}+\varepsilon. ∎

Appendix E Proofs of the main lemmas

E.1 Characterization of ℬ⁡(qdata){\mathcal{B}}(q_{\mathrm{data}}) and 𝒞⁡(qdata){\mathcal{C}}(q_{\mathrm{data}})

The characterization of ℬ⁡(qdata){\mathcal{B}}(q_{\mathrm{data}}) and 𝒞⁡(qdata){\mathcal{C}}(q_{\mathrm{data}}) is summarized in the following lemma.

Lemma 16.

Consider a masking noising process with initial distribution q0=qdataq_{0}=q_{\mathrm{data}}. Let 𝒞⁡(qdata){\mathcal{C}}(q_{\mathrm{data}}) and ℬ⁡(qdata){\mathcal{B}}(q_{\mathrm{data}}) be the total correlation and dual total correlation. Then,

ℬ⁡(qdata)=∫0∞ℐ⁡(t)​𝑑tand𝒞⁡(qdata)=∫0∞(et−1)​ℐ​(t)​𝑑t.\displaystyle{\mathcal{B}}(q_{\mathrm{data}})=\int_{0}^{\infty}{\mathcal{I}}(t)\mathrm{d}t\quad\text{and}\quad{\mathcal{C}}(q_{\mathrm{data}})=\int_{0}^{\infty}(e^{t}-1){\mathcal{I}}(t)\mathrm{d}t.

Consequently, 𝒟⁡(qdata)≤min⁡(ℬ⁡(qdata),𝒞⁡(qdata)){\mathcal{D}}(q_{\mathrm{data}})\leq\min({\mathcal{B}}(q_{\mathrm{data}}),{\mathcal{C}}(q_{\mathrm{data}})).

Proof.

Let p≡p⁡(t)=e−tp\equiv p(t)=e^{-t} be the probability that at time tt a coordinate is unmasked and X⁡(p)≡(X1,…,Xd)≔(xt1,…,xtd)X(p)\equiv(X_{1},\ldots,X_{d})\coloneqq(x_{t}^{1},\ldots,x_{t}^{d}). We also denote Xℛ≔xt−(i,j)X_{{\mathcal{R}}}\coloneqq x_{t}^{-(i,j)} and XR≔(Xi)i∈RX_{R}\coloneqq(X_{i})_{i\in R} for R⊆[d]R\subseteq[d]. With a slight abuse of notation we write ℐ⁡(p)≔ℐ⁡(t⁡(p)){\mathcal{I}}(p)\coloneqq{\mathcal{I}}(t(p)). We have

ℐ⁡(p)≔∑i≠jI⁡(Xi;Xj∣Xℛ)=∑i≠jp2​∑R⊆[d]∖{i,j}p|R|​(1−p)d−2−|R|​I​(Xi;Xj∣XR),{\mathcal{I}}(p)\coloneqq\sum_{i\neq j}\mathrm{I}(X_{i};X_{j}\mid X_{{\mathcal{R}}})=\sum_{i\neq j}p^{2}\sum_{R\subseteq[d]\setminus\{i,j\}}p^{\lvert R\rvert}(1-p)^{d-2-\lvert R\rvert}\mathrm{I}(X_{i};X_{j}\mid X_{R}),

where p2p^{2} appears since for the term I⁡(Xi;Xj∣Xℛ)\mathrm{I}(X_{i};X_{j}\mid X_{\mathcal{R}}) to be non-zero, both XiX_{i} and XjX_{j} must be unmasked. For i∈[d]i\in[d], define

hi​(p)≔∑R⊆[d]∖{i}p|R|​(1−p)d−1−|R|​ℋ​(Xi∣XR),h_{i}(p)\coloneqq\sum_{R\subseteq[d]\setminus\{i\}}p^{\lvert R\rvert}(1-p)^{d-1-\lvert R\rvert}\mathcal{H}(X_{i}\mid X_{R}),

with

d​hi​(p)d​p\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{d}h_{i}(p)}{\mathrm{d}p} =∑R⊆[d]∖{i}[|R|​p|R|−1​(1−p)d−1−|R|−(d−1−|R|)​p|R|​(1−p)d−2−|R|]​ℋ​(Xi∣XR)\displaystyle=\sum_{R\subseteq[d]\setminus\{i\}}\left[\lvert R\rvert p^{\lvert R\rvert-1}(1-p)^{d-1-\lvert R\rvert}-(d-1-\lvert R\rvert)p^{\lvert R\rvert}(1-p)^{d-2-\lvert R\rvert}\right]\mathcal{H}(X_{i}\mid X_{R})
=∑j≠i∑R⊆[d]∖{i,j}p|R|​(1−p)d−2−|R|​(ℋ⁡(Xi∣XR∪{j})−ℋ⁡(Xi∣XR))\displaystyle=\sum_{j\neq i}\sum_{R\subseteq[d]\setminus\{i,j\}}p^{\lvert R\rvert}(1-p)^{d-2-\lvert R\rvert}(\mathcal{H}(X_{i}\mid X_{R\cup\{j\}})-\mathcal{H}(X_{i}\mid X_{R}))
=−∑j≠i∑R⊆[d]∖{i,j}p|R|(1−p)d−2−|R|I(Xi;Xj∣XR).\displaystyle=-\sum_{j\neq i}\sum_{R\subseteq[d]\setminus\{i,j\}}p^{\lvert R\rvert}(1-p)^{d-2-\lvert R\rvert}\mathrm{I}(X_{i};X_{j}\mid X_{R}).

Therefore,

ℐ⁡(p)=∑i=1dp2​(−d​hi​(p)d​p).{\mathcal{I}}(p)=\sum_{i=1}^{d}p^{2}\left(-\frac{\mathrm{d}h_{i}(p)}{\mathrm{d}p}\right).

Since p=e−tp=e^{-t} we have that d​t=−d​pp\mathrm{d}t=-\frac{\mathrm{d}p}{p} and we can write

d​ℋ​(X⁡(p))d​p=∑i=1dhi​(p),\frac{\mathrm{d}\mathcal{H}(X(p))}{\mathrm{d}p}=\sum_{i=1}^{d}h_{i}(p),

therefore,

Since ∑i=1dhi​(1)=∑i=1dℋ⁡(x0i∣x0−i)\sum_{i=1}^{d}h_{i}(1)=\sum_{i=1}^{d}\mathcal{H}(x_{0}^{i}\mid x_{0}^{-i}), we proved the first part:

∫0∞ℐ⁡(t)​𝑑t=ℋ⁡(x0)−∑i=1dℋ⁡(x0i∣x0−i)=ℬ⁡(q0).\int_{0}^{\infty}{\mathcal{I}}(t)\mathrm{d}t=\mathcal{H}(x_{0})-\sum_{i=1}^{d}\mathcal{H}(x_{0}^{i}\mid x_{0}^{-i})={\mathcal{B}}(q_{0}).

We proceed similarly for the total correlation:

∫0∞(et−1)​∑i≠jℐ⁡(t)​dt=∫01(1−p)​∑i=1d(−d​hi​(p)d​p)​dp=−(∑i=1d(1−p)​hi​(p)|01+∫01∑i=1dhi​(p)​dp)\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\infty}(e^{t}-1)\sum_{i\neq j}{\mathcal{I}}(t)\mathrm{d}t=\int_{0}^{1}(1-p)\sum_{i=1}^{d}\left(-\frac{\mathrm{d}h_{i}(p)}{\mathrm{d}p}\right)\mathrm{d}p=-\left(\sum_{i=1}^{d}(1-p)h_{i}(p)\Bigl|_{0}^{1}+\int_{0}^{1}\sum_{i=1}^{d}h_{i}(p)\mathrm{d}p\right)
=∑i=1dℋ⁡(x0i)−ℋ⁡(x0)=𝒞⁡(q0).\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{d}\mathcal{H}(x_{0}^{i})-\mathcal{H}(x_{0})={\mathcal{C}}(q_{0}).

∎

E.2 Proof of Lemma 8

For any i∈[d]i\in[d] and c∈[S]c\in[S], let us define

fi,c(t,xt)≔sT−t(xt⊕ic,xt).\displaystyle f_{i,c}(t,x_{t})\coloneqq s_{T-t}(x_{t}\oplus_{i}c,x_{t}). (107)

The following analysis holds for all i∈[d]i\in[d] and c∈[S]c\in[S], so we safely omit the index i,ci,c in the following analysis, and write it as f⁡(t,xt)f(t,x_{t}).

Consider the case that the backward process {xt}t∈[0,T]∼{q←t}t∈[0,T]\{x_{t}\}_{t\in[0,T]}\sim\{\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t}\}_{t\in[0,T]}, which is a Poisson jump process with generator L←t\overset{\leftarrow}{L}_{t} such that

(L←t​f)​(t,x)\displaystyle\left(\overset{\leftarrow}{L}_{t}f\right)(t,x) =∑y:d_H⁡(y,x)≤1QT−t(y,x)sT−t(y,x)(f(t,y)−f(t,x))\displaystyle=\sum_{y:\ham(y,x)\leq 1}Q_{T-t}(y,x)s_{T-t}(y,x)\big(f(t,y)-f(t,x)\big)
=1S∑y:d_H⁡(y,x)=1sT−t(y,x)(f(t,y)−f(t,x)).\displaystyle=\frac{1}{S}\sum_{y:\ham(y,x)=1}s_{T-t}(y,x)\big(f(t,y)-f(t,x)\big).

By Itô’s formula for Poisson point process in Lemma 6, f⁡(t,xt)f(t,x_{t}) satisfies the following stochastic differential equation: for 0≤ℓ≤t<T0\leq\ell\leq t<T,

f⁡(t,xt)=f⁡(ℓ,xℓ)+∫ℓt[∂tf⁡(s,xs−)+(L←s​f)​(s,xs−)]​𝑑s+Mt,\displaystyle f(t,x_{t})=f(\ell,x_{\ell})+\int_{\ell}^{t}\left[\partial_{t}f(s,x_{s^{-}})+\left(\overset{\leftarrow}{L}_{s}f\right)(s,x_{s^{-}})\right]\mathrm{d}s+M_{t}, (108)

where xs−=limu→s−xsx_{s-}=\lim_{u\to s^{-}}x_{s}, which exists for almost everywhere s∈[0,T)s\in[0,T) under the Lebesgue measure, since we have finite number of jumps almost surely. The compensation process {Mu}u∈[ℓ,t]\{M_{u}\}_{u\in[\ell,t]} in Eqn. (108) is defined as

Mu=∑ys:d_H⁡(ys,xs)=1∫ℓu(f(s,ys)−f(s,xs))(dNsxs,ys−λsxs,ysds),\displaystyle M_{u}=\sum_{y_{s}:\ham(y_{s},x_{s})=1}\int_{\ell}^{u}\big(f(s,y_{s})-f(s,x_{s})\big)\big(\mathrm{d}N_{s}^{x_{s},y_{s}}-\lambda_{s}^{x_{s},y_{s}}\mathrm{d}s\big), (109)

where Nsx,yN_{s}^{x,y} is the counting process of jumps from xx to yy and we write the random counting measure as d​Nsx,y\mathrm{d}N_{s}^{x,y}. We define λsx,y=S−1sT−t(y,x)𝕀{xs−=x}\lambda^{x,y}_{s}=S^{-1}s_{T-t}(y,x){\mathbb{I}}\{x_{s^{-}}\!\!=x\} to be intensity of the process Nsx,yN_{s}^{x,y}. Since xs−=xsx_{s^{-}}=x_{s} almost everywhere s∈(0,T)s\in(0,T) due to the finite number of jumps for each path almost surely, we can rewrite Eqn. (108) as

f⁡(t,xt)−f⁡(ℓ,xℓ)=∫ℓt[∂tf⁡(s,xs)+(L←s​f)​(s,xs)]​𝑑s+Mt.\displaystyle f(t,x_{t})-f(\ell,x_{\ell})=\int_{\ell}^{t}\left[\partial_{t}f(s,x_{s})+\left(\overset{\leftarrow}{L}_{s}f\right)(s,x_{s})\right]\mathrm{d}s+M_{t}. (110)

To further simplify the right hand side, we assert that

∂tf⁡(s,xs)+(L←s​f)​(s,xs)=0.\displaystyle\partial_{t}f(s,x_{s})+\left(\overset{\leftarrow}{L}_{s}f\right)(s,x_{s})=0. (111)

In order to see this, first, recall the definition (107) and direct calculations give

∂tf⁡(s,xs)+(L←s​f)​(s,xs)\displaystyle\partial_{t}f(s,x_{s})+\left(\overset{\leftarrow}{L}_{s}f\right)(s,x_{s})
=∂∂s​(qT−s(xs⊕ic)qT−s​(xs))\displaystyle=\frac{\partial}{\partial s}\left(\frac{q_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i}c)}{q_{T-s}(x_{s})}\right)
+1S∑i′∈[d]∑c′∈[S]sT−s(xs⊕i′c′,xs)(sT−s(xs⊕i′c′⊕ic,xs⊕i′c′)−sT−s(xs⊕ic,xs))\displaystyle\qquad\qquad+\frac{1}{S}\sum_{i^{\prime}\in[d]}\sum_{c^{\prime}\in[S]}s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime},x_{s})\Big(s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime}\oplus_{i}c,x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime})-s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i}c,x_{s})\Big)
=(a)1S∑i′∈[d]∑c′∈[S]sT−s(xs⊕ic,xs)(sT−s(xs⊕i′c′,xs)−sT−s(xs⊕ic⊕i′c′,xs⊕ic))\displaystyle\overset{\mathrm{(a)}}{=}\frac{1}{S}\sum_{i^{\prime}\in[d]}\sum_{c^{\prime}\in[S]}s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i}c,x_{s})\Big(s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime},x_{s})-s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i}c\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime},x_{s}\oplus_{i}c)\Big)
+1S∑i′∈[d]∑c′∈[S]sT−s(xs⊕i′c′,xs)(sT−s(xs⊕i′c′⊕ic,xs⊕i′c′)−sT−s(xs⊕ic,xs))\displaystyle\qquad\qquad+\frac{1}{S}\sum_{i^{\prime}\in[d]}\sum_{c^{\prime}\in[S]}s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime},x_{s})\Big(s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime}\oplus_{i}c,x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime})-s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i}c,x_{s})\Big)
=1S∑i′∈[d]∑c′∈[S](sT−s(xs⊕ic,xs)sT−s(xs⊕i′c′,xs)−sT−s(xs⊕i′c′,xs)sT−s(xs⊕ic,xs))\displaystyle=\frac{1}{S}\sum_{i^{\prime}\in[d]}\sum_{c^{\prime}\in[S]}\Big(s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i}c,x_{s})s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime},x_{s})-s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime},x_{s})s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i}c,x_{s})\Big)
+1S∑i′∈[d]∑c′∈[S](sT−s(xs⊕i′c′,xs)sT−s(xs⊕i′c′⊕ic,xs⊕i′c′)\displaystyle\qquad+\frac{1}{S}\sum_{i^{\prime}\in[d]}\sum_{c^{\prime}\in[S]}\Big(s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime},x_{s})s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime}\oplus_{i}c,x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime})
−sT−s(xs⊕ic,xs)sT−s(xs⊕ic⊕i′c′,xs⊕ic))\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad-s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i}c,x_{s})s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i}c\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime},x_{s}\oplus_{i}c)\Big)
=(b)1S∑i′∈[d]∑c′∈[S](sT−s(xs⊕i′c′⊕ic,xs)−sT−s(xs⊕ic⊕i′c′,xs)),\displaystyle\overset{\mathrm{(b)}}{=}\frac{1}{S}\sum_{i^{\prime}\in[d]}\sum_{c^{\prime}\in[S]}\Big(s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime}\oplus_{i}c,x_{s})-s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i}c\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime},x_{s})\Big),

where in equality (a), we apply the Kolmogorov forward equation on qT−tq_{T-t}; in equality (b), we use the fact that sT−t​(x,y)​sT−t​(y,z)=sT−t​(x,z)s_{T-t}(x,y)s_{T-t}(y,z)=s_{T-t}(x,z) for any x,y,z∈𝒳x,y,z\in{\mathcal{X}}. It is direct to check that the ⊕\oplus operators commute, i.e., for any xs∈𝒳x_{s}\in{\mathcal{X}},

xs⊕i′c′⊕ic=xs⊕ic⊕i′c′.\displaystyle x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime}\oplus_{i}c=x_{s}\oplus_{i}c\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime}.

for i≠i′i\neq i^{\prime}, and the relation holds trivially when i=i′i=i^{\prime}. This relation directly reveals that

∂tf⁡(s,xs)+(L←s​f)​(s,xs)\displaystyle\partial_{t}f(s,x_{s})+\left(\overset{\leftarrow}{L}_{s}f\right)(s,x_{s})
=1S∑i′∈[d]∑c′∈[S](sT−s(xs⊕i′c′⊕ic,xs)−sT−s(xs⊕ic⊕i′c′,xs))=0,\displaystyle=\frac{1}{S}\sum_{i^{\prime}\in[d]}\sum_{c^{\prime}\in[S]}\Big(s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime}\oplus_{i}c,x_{s})-s_{T-s}(x_{s}\oplus_{i}c\oplus_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime},x_{s})\Big)=0,

which completes the proof of Eqn. (111).

Taking u=ℓu=\ell in Eqn. (109), we have Mℓ=0M_{\ell}=0 almost surely, and MuM_{u} is a local martingale for u∈[ℓ,t]u\in[\ell,t] by definition. Recalling Lemma 10, we can bound

sups∈[ℓ,t]supx∈𝒳f⁡(s,x)≤log⁡(S)+max⁡{log⁡((T−t)−1),0}<∞.\displaystyle\sup_{s\in[\ell,t]}\sup_{x\in{\mathcal{X}}}f(s,x)\leq\log(S)+\max\Big\{\log\big((T-t)^{-1}\big),0\Big\}<\infty.

Similarly, for the intensity of the counting process, it satisfies

sups∈[ℓ,t]supx,y∈𝒳λsx,y≤1S​sT−t​(y,x)≤1S​(log⁡(S)+max⁡{log⁡((T−t)−1),0})<∞.\displaystyle\sup_{s\in[\ell,t]}\sup_{x,y\in{\mathcal{X}}}\lambda_{s}^{x,y}\leq\frac{1}{S}s_{T-t}(y,x)\leq\frac{1}{S}\left(\log(S)+\max\Big\{\log\big((T-t)^{-1}\big),0\Big\}\right)<\infty.

Now it is direct to check that

sups∈[ℓ,t]𝔼⁡[|Ms|]≲(t−ℓ)​d​(S−1)⋅sups∈[ℓ,t]supx,y∈𝒳[f⁡(s,x)⋅λsx,y]<∞.\displaystyle\sup_{s\in[\ell,t]}\mathbb{E}[|M_{s}|]\lesssim(t-\ell)d(S-1)\cdot\sup_{s\in[\ell,t]}\sup_{x,y\in{\mathcal{X}}}\left[f(s,x)\cdot\lambda_{s}^{x,y}\right]<\infty.

As a result, we can conclude {Mu}u∈[ℓ,t]\{M_{u}\}_{u\in[\ell,t]} is L1L^{1} and hence a martingale. By the definition of the martingale, we arrive at

𝔼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[Mt]=Mℓ=0.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t\mid\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}[M_{t}]=M_{\ell}=0.

Returning to Eqn. (110), we obtain

𝔼xt∼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[f(t,xt)−f(ℓ,xℓ)]=𝔼xt∼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[Mt]=0.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t\mid\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}\big[f(t,x_{t})-f(\ell,x_{\ell})\big]=\mathbb{E}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t\mid\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}[M_{t}]=0. (112)

Thus, we conclude that

𝔼xt∼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[(sT−ℓ(xℓ⊕ic,xℓ)−sT−t(xt⊕ic,xt))logs^T−ℓ(xℓ⊕ic,xℓ)]\displaystyle{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t|\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}\Big[\big(s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\oplus_{i}c,x_{\ell})-s_{T-t}(x_{t}\oplus_{i}c,x_{t})\big)\log\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\oplus_{i}c,x_{\ell})\Big]
=𝔼xt∼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[f(ℓ,xℓ)−f(t,xt)]⋅logs^T−ℓ(xℓ⊕ic,xℓ)=0,\displaystyle={\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t|\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}\big[f(\ell,x_{\ell})-f(t,x_{t})\big]\cdot\log\widehat{s}_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\oplus_{i}c,x_{\ell})=0,

where we plug in Eqn. (112) in the last line. ∎

E.3 Proof of Lemma 9

The proof of Lemma 9 follows directly from exchanging the order of summation. Specifically, we can write

𝔼xt∼q←t[∑yt:d_H⁡(yt,xt)=1h(sT−t(yt,xt))]\displaystyle{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t}}\left[\sum_{y_{t}:\ham(y_{t},x_{t})=1}h\left(s_{T-t}(y_{t},x_{t})\right)\right]
=𝔼xt∼q←t[∑yt:d_H⁡(yt,xt)=1sT−t(yt,xt)log(sT−t(yt,xt))−sT−t(yt,xt)+1]\displaystyle={\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t}}\left[\sum_{y_{t}:\ham(y_{t},x_{t})=1}s_{T-t}(y_{t},x_{t})\log(s_{T-t}(y_{t},x_{t}))-s_{T-t}(y_{t},x_{t})+1\right]
=𝔼xt∼q←t[∑yt:d_H⁡(yt,xt)=1(qT−t​(yt)qT−t​(xt))log(sT−t(yt,xt))]−𝔼xt∼q←t[∑yt:d_H⁡(yt,xt)=1(qT−t​(yt)qT−t​(xt))]+d(S−1)\displaystyle={\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t}}\left[\sum_{y_{t}:\ham(y_{t},x_{t})=1}\left(\frac{q_{T-t}(y_{t})}{q_{T-t}(x_{t})}\right)\log(s_{T-t}(y_{t},x_{t}))\right]-{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t}}\left[\sum_{y_{t}:\ham(y_{t},x_{t})=1}\left(\frac{q_{T-t}(y_{t})}{q_{T-t}(x_{t})}\right)\right]+d(S-1)
=∑xt∈[S]d∑yt:d_H⁡(yt,xt)=1qT−t(yt)log(sT−t(yt,xt))−∑xt∈[S]d∑yt:d_H⁡(yt,xt)=1qT−t(yt)+d(S−1)\displaystyle=\sum_{x_{t}\in[S]^{d}}\sum_{y_{t}:\ham(y_{t},x_{t})=1}q_{T-t}(y_{t})\log(s_{T-t}(y_{t},x_{t}))-\sum_{x_{t}\in[S]^{d}}\sum_{y_{t}:\ham(y_{t},x_{t})=1}q_{T-t}(y_{t})+d(S-1)
=(a)−∑xt∈[S]d∑yt:d_H⁡(yt,xt)=1qT−t(xt)log(sT−t(yt,xt))−∑yt∈[S]d∑xt:d_H⁡(yt,xt)=1qT−t(yt)+d(S−1)\displaystyle\overset{\mathrm{(a)}}{=}-\sum_{x_{t}\in[S]^{d}}\sum_{y_{t}:\ham(y_{t},x_{t})=1}q_{T-t}(x_{t})\log(s_{T-t}(y_{t},x_{t}))-\sum_{y_{t}\in[S]^{d}}\sum_{x_{t}:\ham(y_{t},x_{t})=1}q_{T-t}(y_{t})+d(S-1)
=−𝔼xt∼q←t[∑yt:d_H⁡(yt,xt)=1log(sT−t(yt,xt))]−d(S−1)+d(S−1)\displaystyle=-{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t}}\left[\sum_{y_{t}:\ham(y_{t},x_{t})=1}\log(s_{T-t}(y_{t},x_{t}))\right]-d(S-1)+d(S-1)
=𝔼xt∼q←t[∑yt:d_H⁡(yt,xt)=1−log(sT−t(yt,xt))],\displaystyle={\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t}}\left[\sum_{y_{t}:\ham(y_{t},x_{t})=1}-\log\left(s_{T-t}(y_{t},x_{t})\right)\right],

where in equality (a), we switch the positions of xtx_{t} and yty_{t} in the summations. ∎

E.4 Proof of Lemma 10

Lemma 10 is a direct consequence of Liang et al. (2025c, Lemma 2). Here, we present a simplified proof based on Proposition 6. It can be easily checked that

αt=1−e−t1+(S−1)​e−t∈(0,1).\displaystyle\alpha_{t}=\frac{1-e^{-t}}{1+(S-1)e^{-t}}\in(0,1).

By Eqn. (59), one has, for d_H⁡(x,y)=1\ham(x,y)=1,

st​(y,x)=𝔼x0∼q0​αtd_H⁡(y,x0)𝔼x0∼q0​αtd_H⁡(x,x0)\displaystyle s_{t}(y,x)=\frac{{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{0}\sim q_{0}}\alpha_{t}^{\ham(y,x_{0})}}{{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{0}\sim q_{0}}\alpha_{t}^{\ham{(x,x_{0})}}} ≤αt−supy,x,x0|d_H(y,x0)−d_H(y,x0)|\displaystyle\leq\alpha_{t}^{-\sup_{y,x,x_{0}}|\ham(y,x_{0})-\ham(y,x_{0})|}
=exp(−log(αt)⋅supy,x,x0|d_H(y,x0)−d_H(y,x0)|)\displaystyle=\exp\left(-\log(\alpha_{t})\cdot\sup_{y,x,x_{0}}|\ham(y,x_{0})-\ham(y,x_{0})|\right)
≤exp(−log(αt)⋅supy,xd_H(y,x))=exp(−log(αt)).\displaystyle\leq\exp\left(-\log(\alpha_{t})\cdot\sup_{y,x}\ham(y,x)\right)=\exp\big(-\log(\alpha_{t})\big).

With similar calculation, one can establish the reversed inequality

st​(y,x)≥exp⁡(log⁡(αt)⋅supy,xd_H⁡(y,x))=exp⁡(log⁡(αt)).\displaystyle s_{t}(y,x)\geq\exp\left(\log(\alpha_{t})\cdot\sup_{y,x}\ham(y,x)\right)=\exp\big(\log(\alpha_{t})\big).

As a result, we conclude

|log⁡(st​(y,x))|≤−log⁡(αt)≲log⁡(S)+max⁡{log⁡(t−1),0}.\displaystyle|\log\big(s_{t}(y,x)\big)|\leq-\log(\alpha_{t})\lesssim\log(S)+\max\big\{\log(t^{-1}),0\big\}.

∎

E.5 Proof of Lemma 11

Let us start by proving the first equation, i.e.,

φi,c(t)=𝖪𝖫(qt∥(Ni,−c)#qt).\displaystyle\varphi_{i,c}(t)=\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}\,\|\,(N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t}).

Recall the definition of φi,c​(t)\varphi_{i,c}(t) that

φi,c​(t)=𝔼xt∼qt​[−log⁡(qt​(Ni,c​(xt))qt​(xt))]=∑xt∈𝒳qt​(x)​log⁡(qt​(x)qt​(Ni,c​(xt))).\displaystyle\varphi_{i,c}(t)=\mathbb{E}_{x_{t}\sim q_{t}}\left[-\log\left(\frac{q_{t}\left(N_{i,c}(x_{t})\right)}{q_{t}(x_{t})}\right)\right]=\sum_{x_{t}\in{\mathcal{X}}}q_{t}(x)\log\left(\frac{q_{t}(x)}{q_{t}\left(N_{i,c}(x_{t})\right)}\right). (113)

As in Eqn. (81), the pushforward measure satisfies

(Ni,−c)#​qt​(x)=qt​(Ni,c​(x)), for any ​x∈𝒳.\displaystyle(N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t}(x)=q_{t}\left(N_{i,c}(x)\right),\text{ for any }x\in{\mathcal{X}}.

As such, we can express Eqn. (113) as

φi,c(t)=∑xt∈𝒳qt(x)log(qt​(x)(Ni,−c)#​qt​(xt))=𝖪𝖫(qt∥(Ni,−c)#qt),\displaystyle\varphi_{i,c}(t)=\sum_{x_{t}\in{\mathcal{X}}}q_{t}(x)\log\left(\frac{q_{t}(x)}{(N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t}(x_{t})}\right)=\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}\,\|\,(N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t}),

which proves the first equation.

For the second relation, the definition of KL divergence gives

−∂∂t𝖪𝖫(qt∥p0)=−∂∂t∑x∈[S]dqt(x)log(qt(x))\displaystyle-\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}\|p_{0})=-\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\sum_{x\in[S]^{d}}q_{t}(x)\log(q_{t}(x)) =−∑x∈[S]dd​qt​(x)d​t(log(qt(x))+1)=−∑x∈[S]dd​qt​(x)d​tlog(qt(x)).\displaystyle=-\sum_{x\in[S]^{d}}\frac{\mathrm{d}q_{t}(x)}{\mathrm{d}t}\big(\log(q_{t}(x))+1\big)=-\sum_{x\in[S]^{d}}\frac{\mathrm{d}q_{t}(x)}{\mathrm{d}t}\log(q_{t}(x)). (114)

Using the Kolmogorov forward equation for the forward noising process, we have

d​qt​(x)d​t=∑y∈𝒳Q(x,y)qt(x)=1S∑y:(y,x)=1qt(y)−d⁡(S−1)Sqt(x).\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{d}q_{t}(x)}{\mathrm{d}t}=\sum_{y\in{\mathcal{X}}}Q(x,y)q_{t}(x)=\frac{1}{S}\sum_{y:\bm{(}y,x)=1}q_{t}(y)-\frac{d(S-1)}{S}q_{t}(x).

Plugging the equation above into Eqn. (114), we arrive at

−∂∂t𝖪𝖫(qt∥p0)\displaystyle-\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}\|p_{0}) =−∑x∈[S]d(∑y:(y,x)=1(1Sqt(y))−d⁡(S−1)Sqt(x))log(qt(x))\displaystyle=-\sum_{x\in[S]^{d}}\left(\sum_{y:\bm{(}y,x)=1}\left(\frac{1}{S}q_{t}(y)\right)-\frac{d(S-1)}{S}q_{t}(x)\right)\log(q_{t}(x))
=−1S∑x∈[S]d∑y:(y,x)=1(qt(y)−qt(x))log(qt(x))\displaystyle=-\frac{1}{S}\sum_{x\in[S]^{d}}\sum_{y:\bm{(}y,x)=1}(q_{t}(y)-q_{t}(x))\log(q_{t}(x))
=−1S∑x∈[S]d∑y:(y,x)=1qt(x)(log(qt(y))−log(qt(x)))=φ(t).\displaystyle=-\frac{1}{S}\sum_{x\in[S]^{d}}\sum_{y:\bm{(}y,x)=1}q_{t}(x)\big(\log(q_{t}(y))-\log(q_{t}(x))\big)=\varphi(t).

In addition, recall φ(t)=1/S∑i∈[d]∑c∈[S]φi,c(t)\varphi(t)=1/S\sum_{i\in[d]}\sum_{c\in[S]}\varphi_{i,c}(t). We reach

φ(t)=1S∑i∈[d]∑c∈[S]𝖪𝖫(qt∥(Ni,−c)#qt)=1S∑i∈[d]∑c∈[S]𝖪𝖫(qt∥(Ni,c)#qt).\displaystyle\varphi(t)=\frac{1}{S}\sum_{i\in[d]}\sum_{c\in[S]}\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}\,\|\,(N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t})=\frac{1}{S}\sum_{i\in[d]}\sum_{c\in[S]}\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}\,\|\,(N_{i,c})_{\#}q_{t}).

∎

E.6 Proof of Lemma 12

Let LL be the time-homogeneous infinitesimal generator of the forward process. Since each coordinate i∈[d]i\in[d] is updated independently in the forward process, we can write L=Li+L−iL=L_{i}+L_{-i}, where LiL_{i} only updates coordinate ii, and L−iL_{-i} updates all other coordinates. It direct to show that LiL_{i} and L−iL_{-i} commute, therefore, we have for any u≥0u\geq 0,

qt+u=qt​eu​Li​eu​L−i,(Ni,−c)#​qt+u=((Ni,−c)#​qt)​eu​Li​eu​L−i,\displaystyle q_{t+u}=q_{t}e^{uL_{i}}e^{uL_{-i}},\quad(N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t+u}=((N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t})e^{uL_{i}}e^{uL_{-i}},

where the second equation is due to the operator Ni,−cN_{i,-c} commutes with the semigroup {eu​L}u≥0\{e^{uL}\}_{u\geq 0}. With this formulation, we reach

φi,c(t+u)=𝖪𝖫(qt+u∥(Ni,−c)#qt+u)≤𝖪𝖫(qteu​Li∥((Ni,−c)#qt)eu​Li),\displaystyle\varphi_{i,c}(t+u)=\mathsf{KL}(q_{t+u}\,\|\,(N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t+u})\leq\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}e^{uL_{i}}\,\|\,((N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t})e^{uL_{i}}), (115)

where in the last inequality, we apply the weak data processing inequality for KL divergence. Since both Ni,−cN_{i,-c} and LiL_{i} only operate on the coordinate ii, we arrive at the decomposition

𝖪𝖫(qteu​Li∥((Ni,−c)#qt)eu​Li)=𝔼x−i∼(qt)−i[𝖪𝖫(qt(⋅|x−i)eu​Li∥((Ni,−c)#qt(⋅|x−i))eu​Li)],\displaystyle\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}e^{uL_{i}}\,\|\,((N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t})e^{uL_{i}})={\mathbb{E}}_{x^{-i}\sim(q_{t})^{-i}}\left[\mathsf{KL}\big(q_{t}(\cdot|x^{-i})e^{uL_{i}}\,\|\,((N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t}(\cdot|x^{-i}))e^{uL_{i}}\big)\right], (116)

where (qt)−i(q_{t})^{-i} is the marginal distribution of qtq_{t} with coordinate ii excluded. Define KuK_{u} to be the transition kernel on [S]×[S][S]\times[S] induced by eu​Lie^{uL_{i}}. It is shown that

Ku​(v1,v2)={1S+(1−1S)​e−uif ​v1=v2;1S​(1−e−u)if ​v1≠v2.\displaystyle K_{u}(v_{1},v_{2})=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{S}+(1-\frac{1}{S})e^{-u}\quad&\text{if }v_{1}=v_{2};\\ \frac{1}{S}(1-e^{-u})\quad&\text{if }v_{1}\neq v_{2}.\end{cases}

It can be directly checked that KuK_{u} is a SS-ary symmetric channel with noise scale σu=(1−S−1)​(1−e−u)\sigma_{u}=(1-S^{-1})(1-e^{-u}). By Makur and Polyanskiy (2018, Proposition 12), a strong data processing inequality holds for the channel KuK_{u}, i.e., for any distribution p,qp,q supported on [S][S],

𝖪𝖫(peu​Li∥qeu​Li)≤η𝖪𝖫(Ku)𝖪𝖫(p∥q),\displaystyle\mathsf{KL}(pe^{uL_{i}}\,\|\,qe^{uL_{i}})\leq\eta_{\mathsf{KL}}(K_{u})\mathsf{KL}(p\,\|\,q),

where η𝖪𝖫​(Ku)\eta_{\mathsf{KL}}(K_{u}) satisfies

η𝖪𝖫​(Ku)≤|1−σu−σuS−1|=1−SS−1​(1−S−1)​(1−e−u)=e−u.\displaystyle\eta_{\mathsf{KL}}(K_{u})\leq\bigg|1-\sigma_{u}-\frac{\sigma_{u}}{S-1}\bigg|=1-\frac{S}{S-1}(1-S^{-1})(1-e^{-u})=e^{-u}.

Taking this strong data processing inequality with Eqn. (116) yields

𝖪𝖫(qteu​Li∥((Ni,−c)#qt)eu​Li)\displaystyle\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}e^{uL_{i}}\|((N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t})e^{uL_{i}}) =𝔼x−i∼(qt)−i[𝖪𝖫(qt(⋅|x−i)eu​Li∥((Ni,−c)#qt(⋅|x−i))eu​Li)]\displaystyle={\mathbb{E}}_{x^{-i}\sim(q_{t})^{-i}}\left[\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}(\cdot|x^{-i})e^{uL_{i}}\,\|\,((N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t}(\cdot|x^{-i}))e^{uL_{i}})\right]
≤𝔼x−i∼(qt)−i[e−u𝖪𝖫(qt(⋅|x−i)∥((Ni,−c)#qt(⋅|x−i))]\displaystyle\leq{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{-i}\sim(q_{t})^{-i}}\left[e^{-u}\,\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}(\cdot|x^{-i})\,\|\,((N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t}(\cdot|x_{-i}))\right]
≤e−u𝔼x−i∼(qt)−i[𝖪𝖫(qt(⋅|x−i)∥((Ni,−c)#qt(⋅|x−i))]\displaystyle\leq e^{-u}\,{\mathbb{E}}_{x^{-i}\sim(q_{t})^{-i}}\left[\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}(\cdot|x^{-i})\,\|\,((N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t}(\cdot|x^{-i}))\right]
=e−u𝖪𝖫(qt∥(Ni,−c)#qt).\displaystyle=e^{-u}\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}\,\|\,(N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t}).

Then, by Eqn. (115), we have

φi,c(t+u)≤𝖪𝖫(qteu​Li∥((Ni,−c)#qt)eu​Li)≤e−u𝖪𝖫(qt∥(Ni,−c)#qt)=e−uφi,c(t),\displaystyle\varphi_{i,c}(t+u)\leq\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}e^{uL_{i}}\,\|\,((N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t})e^{uL_{i}})\leq e^{-u}\mathsf{KL}(q_{t}\,\|\,(N_{i,-c})_{\#}q_{t})=e^{-u}\varphi_{i,c}(t),

which holds for any u≥0u\geq 0. Therefore, the derivative can be bound as

φi,c′​(t)=limu→0+φi,c​(t+u)−φi,c​(t)u≤limu→0+e−uu​φi,c​(t)=−φi,c​(t),\displaystyle\varphi_{i,c}^{\prime}(t)=\lim_{u\to 0^{+}}\frac{\varphi_{i,c}(t+u)-\varphi_{i,c}(t)}{u}\leq\lim_{u\to 0^{+}}\frac{e^{-u}}{u}\varphi_{i,c}(t)=-\varphi_{i,c}(t),

which induces the target result

−φi,c′​(t)≥φi,c​(t).\displaystyle-\varphi_{i,c}^{\prime}(t)\geq\varphi_{i,c}(t).

∎

E.7 Proof of Lemma 14

The proof follows from (Conforti et al., 2025, Lemma 5.2.2). We add the argument below for completeness. Let us define

f(t,xt)≔sT−t(xt⊙ic,xt)𝕀{i∈m(xt)},\displaystyle f(t,x_{t})\coloneqq s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t}){\mathbb{I}}\{i\in m(x_{t})\},

where the dependence on ii and cc is omitted for simplicity. In view of Lemma 6, for 0≤ℓ≤t<T0\leq\ell\leq t<T, we can write

f⁡(t,xt)=f⁡(ℓ,xℓ)+∫ℓt[∂tf⁡(s,xs)+(L←s​f)​(s,xs)]​𝑑s+Mt,\displaystyle f(t,x_{t})=f(\ell,x_{\ell})+\int_{\ell}^{t}\left[\partial_{t}f(s,x_{s})+(\overset{\leftarrow}{L}_{s}f)(s,x_{s})\right]\mathrm{d}s+M_{t},

with generator {L←s}s∈[ℓ,t]\{\overset{\leftarrow}{L}_{s}\}_{s\in[\ell,t]} as follows

(L←s​f)​(s,x)\displaystyle\left(\overset{\leftarrow}{L}_{s}f\right)(s,x) =∑y≠xQT−s​(y,x)​sT−s​(y,x)​(f⁡(s,y)−f⁡(s,x))\displaystyle=\sum_{y\neq x}Q_{T-s}(y,x)s_{T-s}(y,x)\big(f(s,y)-f(s,x)\big)
=∑i′∈m⁡(x)∑c′∈[S]sT−s​(x⊙i′c′,x)​(f⁡(s,x⊙i′c′)−f⁡(s,x)),\displaystyle=\sum_{i^{\prime}\in m(x)}\sum_{c^{\prime}\in[S]}s_{T-s}(x\odot_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime},x)\big(f(s,x\odot_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime})-f(s,x)\big),

and the compensation process {Mu}u∈[ℓ,t]\{M_{u}\}_{u\in[\ell,t]} defined as

Mu=∫ℓu∑i′∈m⁡(xs)∑c′∈[S](f⁡(s,xs⊙i′c′)−f⁡(s,xs))​(d​Nsxs,xs⊙i′c′−λsxs,xs⊙i′c′​𝑑s).\displaystyle M_{u}=\int_{\ell}^{u}\sum_{i^{\prime}\in m(x_{s})}\sum_{c^{\prime}\in[S]}\big(f(s,x_{s}\odot_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime})-f(s,x_{s})\big)\big(\mathrm{d}N_{s}^{x_{s},x_{s}\odot_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime}}-\lambda_{s}^{x_{s},x_{s}\odot_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime}}\mathrm{d}s\big).

With similar argument as in the proof of Lemma 8, one has 𝔼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[Mt]=0,\mathbb{E}_{\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t\mid\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}[M_{t}]=0, which leads to

𝔼xt∼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[f(t,xt)−f(ℓ,xℓ)]=𝔼xt∼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[∫ℓt(∂tf(s,xs)+(L←sf)(s,xs))ds].\displaystyle{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t\mid\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}[f(t,x_{t})-f(\ell,x_{\ell})]={\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t\mid\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}\left[\int_{\ell}^{t}\big(\partial_{t}f(s,x_{s})+(\overset{\leftarrow}{L}_{s}f)(s,x_{s})\big)\mathrm{d}s\right].

Taking derivative with respect to tt on both side, we arrive at

dd​t𝔼xt∼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[f(t,xt)]=𝔼xt∼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[∂tf(t,xt)+(L←tf)(t,xt)].\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t\mid\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}[f(t,x_{t})]={\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t\mid\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}\left[\partial_{t}f(t,x_{t})+(\overset{\leftarrow}{L}_{t}f)(t,x_{t})\right].

Now let us consider each term on the right hand side above separately. By Proposition 6, it obeys that

sT−t​(xt⊙ic,xt)=1eT−t−1​q0​(xt⊙ic)q0​(xt),s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t})=\frac{1}{e^{T-t}-1}\frac{q_{0}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c)}{q_{0}(x_{t})},

and we have

∂∂t​f​(t,xt)=eT−teT−t−1​f​(t,xt).\displaystyle\frac{\partial}{\partial t}f(t,x_{t})=\frac{e^{T-t}}{e^{T-t}-1}f(t,x_{t}).

Next, direct calculations yield

(L←t​f)​(t,xt)\displaystyle(\overset{\leftarrow}{L}_{t}f)(t,x_{t}) =∑i′∈m⁡(xt)∑c′∈[S]sT−t(xt⊙i′c′,xt)(sT−t(xt⊙ic⊙i′c′,xt⊙i′c′)𝕀{i∈m(xt⊙i′c′)}\displaystyle=\sum_{i^{\prime}\in m(x_{t})}\sum_{c^{\prime}\in[S]}s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime},x_{t})\Bigl(s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c\odot_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime},x_{t}\odot_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime}){\mathbb{I}}\{i\in m(x_{t}\odot_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime})\}
−sT−t(xt⊙ic,xt)𝕀{i∈m(xt)})\displaystyle\hskip 100.00015pt-s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t}){\mathbb{I}}\{i\in m(x_{t})\}\Bigr)
=1eT−t−1​f​(t,xt)​(∑i′∈m⁡(xt)∖{i}∑c′∈[S]q0(xt⊙ic⊙i′c′)q0​(xt⊙ic)−∑i′∈m⁡(xt)∑c′∈[S]q0​(xt⊙i′c′)q0​(xt))\displaystyle\quad=\frac{1}{e^{T-t}-1}f(t,x_{t})\left(\sum_{i^{\prime}\in m(x_{t})\setminus\{i\}}\sum_{c^{\prime}\in[S]}\frac{q_{0}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c\odot_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime})}{q_{0}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c)}-\sum_{i^{\prime}\in m(x_{t})}\sum_{c^{\prime}\in[S]}\frac{q_{0}(x_{t}\odot_{i^{\prime}}c^{\prime})}{q_{0}(x_{t})}\right)
=1eT−t−1​f​(t,xt)​(|m⁡(xt)∖{i}|−|m⁡(xt)|)=−1eT−t−1​f​(t,xt).\displaystyle\quad=\frac{1}{e^{T-t}-1}f(t,x_{t})(|m(x_{t})\setminus\{i\}|-|m(x_{t})|)=-\frac{1}{e^{T-t}-1}f(t,x_{t}).

Putting everything together leads to

dd​t𝔼xt∼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[f(t,xt)]=𝔼xt∼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[f(t,xt)],\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t\mid\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}[f(t,x_{t})]={\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t\mid\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}[f(t,x_{t})],

and therefore,

𝔼xt∼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[f(t,xt)]=et−ℓ⋅f(ℓ,xℓ).\displaystyle{\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t\mid\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}[f(t,x_{t})]=e^{t-\ell}\cdot f(\ell,x_{\ell}).

Finally, in view of the relation Pr⁡(xti=MASK∣xℓi=MASK)=1−eT−t1−eT−ℓ\Pr(x_{t}^{i}=\mathrm{MASK}\mid x_{\ell}^{i}=\mathrm{MASK})=\frac{1-e^{T-t}}{1-e^{T-\ell}}, we conclude the following

𝔼xt∼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[sT−t(xt⊙ic,xt)𝕀{i∈m(xt)}]=et−ℓ⋅sT−ℓ(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)𝕀{i∈m(xℓ)}=𝔼xt∼q←t|ℓ(⋅∣xℓ)[sT−t(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ)𝕀{i∈m(xt)}],\displaystyle\begin{aligned} {\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t\mid\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}\big[s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t})\,{\mathbb{I}}\{i\in m(x_{t})\}\big]&=e^{t-\ell}\cdot s_{T-\ell}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell}){\mathbb{I}}\{i\in m(x_{\ell})\}\\ &={\mathbb{E}}_{x_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{t\mid\ell}(\cdot\mid x_{\ell})}\big[s_{T-t}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell})\,{\mathbb{I}}\{i\in m(x_{t})\}\big],\end{aligned}

which completes the proof of the desired result. ∎

Appendix F Proofs of the auxiliary lemmas

F.1 Proof of Lemma 2

For a continuous random variable UU in ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d} with density function pUp_{U} with respect to Lebesgue measure, define the differential entropy of UU as

ℋdiff(U)=−∫ℝdpUlog(pU)dx,\displaystyle{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(U)=-\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}p_{U}\log(p_{U})\mathrm{d}x, (117)

where we adopt the convention 0​log⁡(0)=00\log(0)=0 again. By definition of mutual information, we have

I⁡(W,W+εnoise)\displaystyle I(W;W+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}) =ℋdiff​(W+εnoise)−ℋdiff​(W+εnoise∣W)\displaystyle={\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(W+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}})-{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(W+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}\mid W)
=(a)​ℋdiff​(W+εnoise)−𝔼w​[ℋdiff​(w+εnoise∣W=w)]\displaystyle\overset{\mathrm{(a)}}{=}{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(W+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}})-\mathbb{E}_{w}\big[{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(w+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}\mid W=w)\big]
=(b)​ℋdiff​(W+εnoise)−𝔼w​[ℋdiff​(εnoise∣W=w)]\displaystyle\overset{\mathrm{(b)}}{=}{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(W+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}})-\mathbb{E}_{w}\big[{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}\mid W=w)\big]
=(c)​ℋdiff​(W+εnoise)−ℋdiff​(εnoise),\displaystyle\overset{\mathrm{(c)}}{=}{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(W+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}})-{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}), (118)

where in (a), we use the chain rule of differential entropy; in (b), we apply the translation invariance property, i.e., ℋdiff​(U)=ℋdiff​(c0+U){\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(U)={\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(c_{0}+U) for any constant c0c_{0}; in (c), we use the condition that εnoise⟂⟂W\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}\perp\!\!\!\perp W.

Denote the Gaussian density function with mean 00 and variance σ2​Id\sigma^{2}I_{d} as ϕσ​(⋅)\phi_{\sigma}(\cdot). Since εnoise∼𝒩⁡(0,σ2​Id)\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}\sim{\mathcal{N}}(0,\sigma^{2}I_{d}), we can compute with Equation 117 that

ℋdiff​(εnoise)\displaystyle{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}) =−∫ℝdϕσ(x)log(ϕσ(x))dx\displaystyle=-\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\phi_{\sigma}(x)\log\big(\phi_{\sigma}(x)\big)\mathrm{d}x
=−∫ℝdϕσ(x)(−d2log(2πσ2)−‖x‖222​σ2)dx\displaystyle=-\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\phi_{\sigma}(x)\left(-\frac{d}{2}\log(2\pi\sigma^{2})-\frac{\|x\|_{2}^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)\mathrm{d}x
=d2​log⁡(2​π​σ2)+𝔼⁡[‖εnoise‖22]2​σ2\displaystyle=\frac{d}{2}\log(2\pi\sigma^{2})+\frac{\mathbb{E}[\|\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}\|_{2}^{2}]}{2\sigma^{2}}
=d2​log⁡(2​π​e​σ2),\displaystyle=\frac{d}{2}\log(2\pi e\sigma^{2}), (119)

where ∥⋅∥2\|\cdot\|_{2} is the Euclidean norm in ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}. For ℋdiff​(W+εnoise){\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(W+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}), notice that

Var⁡[W+εnoise]=Var⁡[W]+Var⁡[εnoise]+2​Cov​[W,εnoise]=Var⁡[W]+σ2​Id.\displaystyle\mathrm{Var}\big[W+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}\big]=\mathrm{Var}[W]+\mathrm{Var}[\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}]+2\,\mathrm{Cov}\big[W,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}\big]=\mathrm{Var}[W]+\sigma^{2}I_{d}.

By Cover (1999, Page 255), for distributions with the same finite variance, ℋdiff{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}} is maximized at the centered Gaussian random variable. Therefore, we have

ℋdiff​(W+εnoise)\displaystyle{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(W+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}) ≤ℋdiff​(𝒩⁡(0,Var⁡[W]+σ2​Id))=d2​log⁡(2​π​e)+12​log⁡(det⁡(Var⁡[W]+σ2​Id)),\displaystyle\leq{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}\Big({\mathcal{N}}\big(0,\mathrm{Var}[W]+\sigma^{2}I_{d}\big)\Big)=\frac{d}{2}\log(2\pi e)+\frac{1}{2}\log\left(\mathrm{det}\big(\mathrm{Var}[W]+\sigma^{2}I_{d}\big)\right),

where det⁡(⋅)\mathrm{det}(\cdot) is the determinant of matrices, and the calculation is the same as in Equation 119. Since Var⁡[W]\mathrm{Var}[W] is a positive semidefinite matrix, we can apply the matrix inequality that

log⁡(det⁡(Var⁡[W]+σ2​Id))\displaystyle\log\left(\mathrm{det}\big(\mathrm{Var}[W]+\sigma^{2}I_{d}\big)\right) =d​log⁡(σ2)+log⁡(det⁡(Id+Var⁡[W/σ2]))\displaystyle=d\log(\sigma^{2})+\log\left(\mathrm{det}\big(I_{d}+\mathrm{Var}[W/\sigma^{2}]\big)\right)
≤d​log⁡(σ2)+Tr⁡(Var⁡[W/σ2])\displaystyle\leq d\log(\sigma^{2})+\mathrm{Tr}\left(\mathrm{Var}[W/\sigma^{2}]\right)
=d​log⁡(σ2)+Tr⁡(Var⁡[W])σ2,\displaystyle=d\log(\sigma^{2})+\frac{\mathrm{Tr}\left(\mathrm{Var}[W]\right)}{\sigma^{2}},

which leads to

ℋdiff​(W+εnoise)\displaystyle{\mathcal{H}}^{\mathrm{diff}}(W+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}}) ≤d2​log⁡(2​π​e​σ2)+Tr⁡(Var⁡[W])2​σ2.\displaystyle\leq\frac{d}{2}\log(2\pi e\sigma^{2})+\frac{\mathrm{Tr}\left(\mathrm{Var}[W]\right)}{2\sigma^{2}}. (120)

Plugging Eqns. (119) and (120) into Equation 118, we conclude that

I⁡(W,W+εnoise)≤d2​log⁡(2​π​e​σ2)+Tr⁡(Var⁡[W])2​σ2−d2​log⁡(2​π​e​σ2)=Tr⁡(Var⁡[W])2​σ2.\displaystyle I(W;W+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{noise}})\leq\frac{d}{2}\log(2\pi e\sigma^{2})+\frac{\mathrm{Tr}\left(\mathrm{Var}[W]\right)}{2\sigma^{2}}-\frac{d}{2}\log(2\pi e\sigma^{2})=\frac{\mathrm{Tr}\left(\mathrm{Var}[W]\right)}{2\sigma^{2}}.

∎

F.2 Proof of Lemma 3

For X∼Bin⁡(n,1/2)X\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n,1/2), its pmf is given by

ℙ⁡(X=x)=(nx)​(12)n∝(nx).\displaystyle\mathbb{P}(X=x)={n\choose x}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n}\propto{n\choose x}.

Notice that our desired bound is equivalent to the following equation:

∑x:xmod2=0(nx)=∑x:xmod2=1(nx),\displaystyle\sum_{x:x\bmod 2=0}{n\choose x}=\sum_{x:x\bmod 2=1}{n\choose x},

which follows from the binomial theorem for 0=(1−1)n0=(1-1)^{n}. ∎

F.3 Proof of Lemma 13

The CTMC (88) in the lemma statement can be decomposed into dd independent CTMCs for each coordinate. For coordinates ii such that xtki≠MASKx_{t_{k}}^{i}\neq\mathrm{MASK} clearly neither Equation 88 nor Algorithm 1 makes a change. Next, we fix i∈m⁡(xtk)i\in m(x_{t_{k}}). First, we compute the probability that the ii-th coordinate remains masked for ytk+1y_{t_{k+1}}:

Pr⁡(ytk+1i=MASK∣ytk)\displaystyle\Pr(y_{t_{k+1}}^{i}=\mathrm{MASK}\mid y_{t_{k}}) =exp(∫tktk+1(−∑c∈[S]s^T−tk(ytk⊙ic,ytk)eT−tk−1eT−t−1)dt)\displaystyle=\exp\left(\int_{t_{k}}^{t_{k+1}}\left(-\sum_{c\in[S]}\widehat{s}_{T-t_{k}}(y_{t_{k}}\odot_{i}c,y_{t_{k}})\frac{e^{T-t_{k}}-1}{e^{T-t}-1}\right)\mathrm{d}t\right)
=exp⁡(Q^ki​(MASK)​Δk)\displaystyle=\exp(\widehat{Q}_{k}^{i}(\mathrm{MASK})\Delta_{k})
=𝒫k,\displaystyle={\mathcal{P}}_{k},

where Q^ki​(MASK)\widehat{Q}_{k}^{i}(\mathrm{MASK}), Δk\Delta_{k}, and 𝒫k{\mathcal{P}}_{k} are defined in Algorithm 1. Next, for c∈[S]c\in[S] we can write

Pr⁡(ytk+1i=c∣xtk)=Pr⁡(xtk+1i=c∣xtk​ and ​xtk+1i≠MASK)​(1−𝒫k).\Pr(y_{t_{k+1}}^{i}=c\mid x_{t_{k}})=\Pr(x_{t_{k+1}}^{i}=c\mid x_{t_{k}}\text{ and }x_{t_{k+1}}^{i}\neq\mathrm{MASK})(1-{\mathcal{P}}_{k}).

Since for any t∈[tk,tk+1)t\in[t_{k},t_{k+1}) the rates Q^t​(x,x⊙ic)\widehat{Q}_{t}(x,x\odot_{i}c) are proportional to Q^ki​(c)\widehat{Q}_{k}^{i}(c), we get that

Pr⁡(ytk+1i=c∣xtk​ and ​ytk+1i≠MASK)=Q^ki​(c)∑b∈[S]Q^ki​(b),\Pr(y_{t_{k+1}}^{i}=c\mid x_{t_{k}}\text{ and }y_{t_{k+1}}^{i}\neq\mathrm{MASK})=\frac{\widehat{Q}_{k}^{i}(c)}{\sum_{b\in[S]}\widehat{Q}_{k}^{i}(b)},

which matches the expression in Algorithm 1. Therefore, the distribution of ytk+1y_{t_{k+1}} defined by the CTMC matches the distribution of xtk+1x_{t_{k+1}} from the algorithm. ∎

In view of the definition of D⁡(⋅,⋅)D(\cdot,\cdot), one can write

sT−t​(xt⊙ic,xt)​D​(sT−t​(xℓ⊙ic,xℓ),sT−t​(xt⊙ic,xt))\displaystyle s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t})D\left(s_{T-t}(x_{\ell}\odot_{i}c,x_{\ell}),s_{T-t}(x_{t}\odot_{i}c,x_{t})\right)

=∑i∈[d]𝔼yℓ,yt∼q←ℓ,t​log⁡q0​(yt)​q0​(yℓ⊙iMASK)q0​(yt⊙iMASK)​q0​(yℓ⊙iyti),\displaystyle\quad=\sum_{i\in[d]}{\mathbb{E}}_{y_{\ell},y_{t}\sim\overset{\leftarrow}{q}_{\ell,t}}\log\frac{q_{0}(y_{t})q_{0}(y_{\ell}\odot_{i}\mathrm{MASK})}{q_{0}(y_{t}\odot_{i}\mathrm{MASK})q_{0}(y_{\ell}\odot_{i}y_{t}^{i})}, (121)

where in the second line, we used the definition of the score function along with the natural bijection between the sets {(x,i,c), for x∈𝒳, i∈m(x), and c∈[S]}\{(x,i,c)\text{, for }x\in{\mathcal{X}}\text{, }i\in m(x)\text{, and }c\in[S]\} and {(y,i), for y∈𝒳 and i∉m(y)}\{(y,i)\text{, for }y\in{\mathcal{X}}\text{ and }i\notin m(y)\} to change the measure under the expectation:
